function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Dates are taken from the official festival calendars (or their most recent announcements) and may shift slightly as the year progresses—always double‑check the event’s own site for the latest updates.

| # | Festival | Typical Dates (2026) | Location | What It’s About | Ticket Info / Where to Buy |
|---|----------|----------------------|----------|-----------------|----------------------------|
| 1 | **Burning Man** | Aug 5–12, 2026 | Black Rock City, NV (Black Rock Desert) | An immersive art & community gathering where participants create a temporary city built around radical self‑expression, art installations, and communal living. | Early‑bird tickets start in May; general sale in June. Purchase via the official Burning Man website. |
| 2 | **Taste of Chicago** | Aug 18–21, 2026 | Grant Park, Chicago, IL | One of the world’s largest street food festivals featuring dozens of vendors, live music, and family‑friendly activities. | Tickets sold through the Taste of Chicago site; some free entry days. |
| 3 | **Newport Folk Festival** | Sep 9–11, 2026 | Newport, RI | A three‑day celebration of folk, bluegrass, and Americana music with headliners, workshops, and a kids’ area. | General admission and VIP packages available on the Newport Folk Festival website. |
| 4 | **Austin Music Fest** | Sep 15–17, 2026 | Austin, TX | A multi‑genre festival featuring indie, hip‑hop, electronic, and country acts across several venues. | Tickets on the Austin Music Fest site; early‑bird discounts in August. |
| 5 | **Newport Jazz Festival** | Oct 7–9, 2026 | Newport, RI | A historic jazz festival showcasing legends, emerging artists, and jam sessions. | Tickets via the Newport Jazz Festival site; early‑bird pricing in September. |

### Quick Tips for Planning

| Tip | Why It Helps |
|-----|--------------|
| **Buy early‑bird tickets** | Prices rise dramatically once general sale opens. |
| **Check accommodation options** | Many festivals offer on‑site lodging or partner hotels; booking early secures better rates. |
| **Read the festival FAQ** | Policies on camping, food, and COVID‑19 protocols vary widely. |
| **Plan transportation** | Some festivals are in remote locations (e.g., Burning Man); consider carpooling or shuttle services. |

---

#### How to Stay Updated

- **Official Websites** – Most festivals post a “Tickets” page with exact dates and pricing tiers.  
- **Social Media** – Follow the festival’s official Twitter/X or Instagram accounts for real‑time announcements.  
- **Event Aggregators** – Sites like Songkick, Bandsintown, or Eventbrite often list upcoming lineups and ticket links.  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like deeper details on any particular festival (lineup, travel tips, budget breakdown, etc.)!
